## Game
Game: Cube Cash Tycoon - Watch cubes roll down your conveyor, cash in, and buy droppers and speed upgrades to grow your tiny factory!
Core loop: Each player gets a bright plot with a dropper that spawns a 1-cash cube every 2 seconds onto a conveyor. The conveyor carries cubes to a collector at the end, and the server adds each cube's value to the player's Cash leaderstat and destroys the cube. Two buy pads sit off to the side of the walking area: a second dropper for 25 cash and a faster conveyor for 50 cash. Touching a pad with enough cash buys the upgrade once, so income climbs and the numbers go up.
Acceptance: The map (baseplate and the player's plot with dropper, conveyor, collector and two buy pads) is built from parts at startup and the 'map_built' counter is 1; The player spawns on their plot within a few seconds, and 'plot_assigned' is 1; 'cubes_dropped' increases within the first 2 seconds and keeps increasing roughly every 2 seconds; 'cubes_collected' increases as cubes reach the collector, and the Cash leaderstat rises; Touching a buy pad with insufficient cash does nothing; with enough cash it deducts the cost once and increments 'dropper_bought' or 'conveyor_bought'; The HUD shows the current Cash and updates as it changes; Walking from spawn does not trigger the buy pads accidentally, and the cube count stays under the cap; No errors or warnings appear in the output; At startup the plaza (stone tiles, fountain, lamp posts, trees) and 6 plots in a ring exist; 'plaza_built' is 1, 'themes_built' is 6 and 'map_built' is 1; Each plot has a distinct theme floor material and color plus 3-5 decoration props (lollipops, lava cracks, crystals, palm trees, neon strips, cacti), and no part is default grey; rails, dropper bodies and pads use theme colors; Players spawn in the plaza, not on a plot, and cubes_dropped stays 0 until a plot is claimed; Each free plot shows a glowing gate with a BillboardGui reading 'Claim <Theme> Plot'; Walking onto a gate claims that plot: the sign shows the player's name, the gate hides, 'plots_claimed' and 'plot_assigned' increase, and 'cubes_dropped' starts rising about every 2 seconds; A player who does not claim within 20 seconds is auto-claimed to the nearest free plot ('auto_claims' increases) and the dropper starts; ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades has 10 upgrades with unique ids, every requires id exists, and the first purchase (Dropper 2) costs 10; After claiming a plot, only the Dropper 2 pad is visible on that plot, with a billboard showing its name and '$10'; Within about 10 seconds of claiming, Cash reaches 10 and the Dropper 2 pad turns the plot accent color; Touching Dropper 2 with enough cash deducts 10 exactly once, the pad vanishes, the Silver, Speed 1 and Dropper 3 pads appear, and 'upgrades_bought' increments; Touching a pad with insufficient cash, or whose parent is not owned, does nothing and deducts nothing; After Dropper 2 is bought, two cubes spawn per drop cycle and 'cubes_dropped' rises faster

## Feature request
Fix this bug: Make the tutorial advance through claim, first cash-in, Dropper 2 buy, open SHOP, and buy a tier upgrade. Show the arrow and a visible Beam from the player to each target (the census must show beams > 0). Re-show a stuck step's hint after 15s. Fire shop_opened when the SHOP panel opens. Tutorial steps must reach 5+ in a 60s playtest, and the stale step-4 text must match the real action.

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull. Also keep the second purchase within about 20-30s of idle income, by raising per-item value or lowering the price, so the shop and later upgrades get exercised.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.
- Keep the time to first core-loop activity well inside the playtest window (the probe may last only ~6-15s). Any auto-claim or auto-start fallback should fire within a few seconds (about 3-5s, not 20s), and claim gates should sit near the spawn area, not far outside the plaza. An idle player must still reach the loop quickly. Keep the spec's auto-claim delay and the tested window consistent so the plaza state can still be observed before the claim.
- Budget the whole first-payout path, not just the claim: claim delay + first spawn + conveyor travel (length / speed) should land the first cash-in within about 3-4s of the claim. Use a short, fast conveyor, spawn the first item immediately on claim, and don't leave this borderline.
- Keep tutorial text consistent with the actual flow (e.g. don't say "walk to a gate" if auto-claim happens within seconds). Tutorial steps must be advanced by events that actually occur, or the player is left without guidance. Add a time-based fallback so a step can't stall. Make the steps lead the player to every key feature (buy pad, shop), and check that the guide beam or arrow actually appears (its census count is above 0).
- Feedback should be audible and visible: use verified sound ids from the shared asset table, not weak built-in rbxasset wavs. Add particles or ambient sparkle, and set the bloom threshold low enough that Neon parts glow.
- Shared effect helpers (burst, shake, sound, FOV punch) only matter if gameplay code calls them. Wire each helper to a real event (collect, buy, rebirth, big upgrade) and check that its counter is above 0 after a playtest. Big moments deserve stronger feedback than routine ones: camera shake, a shockwave ring, or a larger popup.

## Luau and Roblox APIs
- The base place is empty: build the map from code (Instance.new Parts, Anchored = true, parented to Workspace).
- Get services with game:GetService("Players") etc.; use task.wait / task.spawn / task.delay, never wait / spawn / delay.
